notifications were accompanied by a statement indic ating the reasons for the delay in laying. In 
some of the cases the delay has been quite long. Th e observations/recommendations of the 
Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: -    
 
 
(i) Ministry of Agriculture 
 (Department of Agriculture and Cooperation) 
 
Out of 9 notifications (Sl. Nos. 1 to 9) laid by th e Ministry of Agriculture (Department of 
Agriculture and Cooperation)  3 notifications (Sl. Nos. 5 to 7)  were found to ha ve  been delayed, 
by four months, although these notifications were accompanied by Delay Statements. The reasons 
of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The notifications was sent on 8 
th  November, 2010 to the Government of India Press fo r 
its publication in the Gazette of India (Extraordin ary) Part II, Section 3, Sub-Section (ii) and also 
for printing of 200 copies of each notifications fo r laying in both Houses of Parliament. 
Although, the order was published on the 8 th  November, 2010 in the Gazette of India 
(Extraordinary) but printed copies were not available/provided by the press in time. These Orders 
were required to be laid in both the Houses  of the  Parliament during the winter session, 2010. 
The same could not be laid due to paucity of time.” 

 
The Committee are not convinced by the reason given  for delay by the Ministry that 
the printed copies of Gazette Notifications could n ot be made available in time. Ministry 
should have mentioned the date when printed copies were to be given to it by the 
Government of India Press as also the efforts made by it to get the printing expedited. Delay 
could have been avoided, had adequate precaution be en taken by the Ministry in this 
regard. The Committee feel  that the Ministry of Ag riculture  did not take it with required 
seriousness. Such delays in future, particularly on  account of delay in receiving printed 
copies of notifications will not be acceptable to t he Committee. Ministry would have to 
adhere to the time schedule for notifying as well a s laying of papers as prescribed in 
Committee’s 131 st  Report. 
 
 
 
 
(ii) Ministry of Commerce and  Industry 
  
(Department of Commerce and Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion) 
 

 Ministry of  Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce) have laid 5 notifications, 
out of which two notifications (Sl. Nos. 18 and 20)  have been delayed by 4 months and six 
months respectively. There is no delay statement appended to both of them. 
 
 Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion have  laid 9 notifications, 5 of these 
notifications have been delayed. Out of 5 delayed n otifications only 3 were accompanied with 
delay statements; 2 notifications had no delay statements appended to them. The Committee notes 
that in majority of cases delay period range from 3  to 6 months. But in two cases Sl. Nos. 28 and 
29) there is delay of one year and seven months and  2 years. The reasons of delay are given as 
under:- 
 
 “Electrical Wires, Cable Appliances and Protection  Devices and Accessories (Quality 
Control) Amendment Order, 2009 (S.O. 512 (E) of 200 9) was published in Gazette of India, 
Extraordinary, Part-II, Section 3 (ii) dated 19 Feb ruary, 2009. Later it was decided to rescind the 
said Quality Control Order No. S.O. 512 (E) of 2009 , on the request of Industry Associations as 
they faced some procedural difficulties in implemen ting this order within time limit fixed in the 
said order and therefore could not be sent to Rajya Sabha Secretariat to be laid on the Table of the 
House. The said Quality Control Order was rescinded  vide Gazette Notification No. S.O. 2058 
(E) dated 07.08.2009 Electrical Wires, Cables, Appl iances and Protection Devices and 
Accessories (Quality Control) Amendment Order, 2009. 

 After cross verification with related records, it has been observed that the subject 
notifications were not laid on the Table of the Hou ses because the requisite number of copies 
(authenticated + additional copies) as required under the procedure were not sent at the time. This 
lapse was purely unintentional and occurred due to oversight. The delay is deeply regretted and 
may be condoned. It is also ensured that such lapse would not recur in future.” 
 
The Committee have noted the reply given by the Min istry of Commerce and 
Industry (Department of Industrial Policy and Promo tion) that the notifications could not 
be laid due to inadvertence. The Committee hope tha t the Ministry would in future be 
careful about laying of its papers and see that per sons responsible for this remain vigilant 
about it. As regards reason for decision to rescind  the earlier notification on the feedback 
from the industry within no time after it was issue d, shows that required consultation were 
not done with the Industry before it was notified. This should be avoided in future because 
such delays might lead to avoidable complications.  
 
(iii) Ministry of Communication and Information Tec hnology 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
 Ministry of Communication and Information Technolo gy (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid one notification (Sl.  No. 35) which has been delayed by 3 
months. There is delay statement attached to it which reads as under:- 

 
 “The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is a statutory body set up under the 
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997. In  exercise of the powers conferred upon it 
under section 36 of the TRAI Act, 1997, the Authori ty may, by notification, make regulations 
consistent with the Act and the Rules made there un der to carry out the purposes of the Act. 
Under section 37 of the Act, the regulations notifi ed by TRAI are required to be laid before each 
House of Parliament. 
 The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) i n exercise of the powers conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 36, read with sub-clauses (i), (iii) and (v) of clause (b) of sub-section 
(1) of section 11 of the TRAI Act, 1997 notified “Telecommunication Mobile Number Portability 
(Second Amendment) Regulations, 2010.” The said Reg ulation was issued on 24.11.2010. On 
receipt of the copies of the Gazette Notification o n 7 
th  December, 2010 from the Government of 
India Press, TRAI sent the Regulation to the Depart ment on 8 th  December, 2010. However, the 
Parliament was adjourned sine die on 13 th  December, 2010 and the Regulation could not be lai d 
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during the Winter Session 2010 of Parliament.” 
 
The Committee are not inclined to accept the late r eceipt of printed copies from the 
Government of India Press as a valid reason for a d elayed laying of notifications etc. The 
Ministry of Communications and Information Technolo gy  should in future ensure that all 
its papers were laid before the House as prescribed in the Committee’s 131 st  Report. 
 

(iv) Ministry of Consumer Affairs 
 (Department of Food and Public Distribution) 
 
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs (Department of Food a nd Public Distribution have laid 7 
notifications (Sl. Nos. 45 to 51). Two of these (Sl . Nos. 49 and 50) had been delayed by three 
months and one year respectively. But the delay sta tement was appended with only one of the 
delayed notifications.  
  
   The Committee take strong exception to the Ministry ’s failure to lay the delay 
Statement. It fails to understand how in one case Delay Statement was laid and in other case 
it was not. It shows that papers before being sent for laying were not being seen by senior 
officers and it is being taken as a routine work. T he Committee feel that it amounts to 
restricting Parliament’s right to be informed about  delegated legislation and views it 
seriously. This should be avoided in future without a genuine cause.  
 
(v) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 21 notific ations and one notification (Sl. No. 53) 
has been delayed by 5 months and the delay statemen t is appended to the notification. The 
reasons of delay is given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 

 “The notification could not be laid before both th e Houses of Parliament within the 
prescribed period as the required number of copies of the notification could not be made available 
within the stipulated time frame from the Governmen t Press. Accordingly, the notifications are 
being laid before both the Houses of Parliament now”.  
 
The Committee take serious view in cases where the delay is attributed to non-
availability of the required number of copies of no tifications. Ministries have been taking 
recourse to this plea very frequently. This possibility  should have been foreseen well in time 
and adequate arrangements made in respect thereof. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
must ensure that such delay don’t recur in future.  
 
(vi) Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 
 Ministry of Environment and Forests have laid 14 n otifications (Sl. Nos. 73 to 86) out of 
which 8 notifications (Sl. Nos. 75-81 and 84), have  been delayed by 3 to 9 months. Delay 
statement has been attached to none of these.  
 
The Committee are anguished to see that  the Minist ry of Environment and Forests 
not only had delayed the laying of 8 of its notific ations, it had also failed to lay delay 
statement that  it is required to do so. The Commit tee in this connection invite attention to 
its recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report. The Committee have decided to take a 

serious view in such failures particularly by a Min istry like Environment and Forests that 
lays fairly large number of notifications etc. duri ng every session. The Ministry should 
know that such failure in laying papers amounts to curtailing the Parliament’s right to be 
informed about subordinate legislations. 
 
(vii) Ministry of External Affairs  
 
 The only notification that the Ministry of Externa l Affairs have laid is delayed by 3 
months and no delay statement is  appended to it. 
  
 The Ministry must be aware of the Committee’s recom mendations in its 135 Report 
that in case of delay in laying, notifications shou ld be accompanied with delay statement. 
The Ministry should appreciate the constitutional significance behind that requirement that  
flows from the principle of parliamentary control o f subordinate legislations. It therefore, 
should take care that repetition of such delay is avoided in future. 
 
 
(viii)   Ministry of Finance 
 
(A)  (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 

  The Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Aff airs) have laid 4 notifications  on 
the Table of the House. Out of these 2 notification s (Sl. Nos. 88 and 89) have been delayed. 
There is delay of 3 months in each case and no delay statement is  appended to them. 
 
 The Committee take a serious view not only about t he delay in laying of two of its 
notifications on the Table of the House but also fa ilure to append the delay statement with 
them. The Ministry/Department must know about the p ossible implications of failing to 
meet this requirement. It must ensure to append a delay statement in all cases in future. 
 
 
(B)  (Department of Financial Services) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial S ervices) have laid 32 notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 92 – 123). Out of these 30 notifications  have  been  delayed with delay period of 3 to 5 
months and no delay statement is attached  with the m except with one notification (Sl. No. 121). 
The reasons forwarded by the Ministry for delay in this case is as under:- 
 
 “The Gazette Notification No. PW:IRS:1:3513:2010 d ated 17.09.2010  regarding 
amendment in Regulations 2(o), 8,9 & 10 of the Cana ra Bank Employees’ Pension  Regulations 
1995 was published in the Gazette of India dated No vember 20 – November 26, 2010. The Bank 
has stated that they received the copies of Gazette Notification from the Controller of Publication, 

Department of Publication, Ministry of Urban Develo pment on 28.12.2010. As a result of this, 
the said Notification could not be laid on the Tabl e of the House during Winter Session, 2010 of 
Parliament.” 
 
 This is just not acceptable to the Committee that 30 out of 32 notifications laid by the 
Ministry did not have delay statements. While there  may be a reason for the delay there 
cannot be any reason for not furnishing reason for that. The Ministry must understand the 
implications for not doing so regularly and in such a large number of cases. 
 
 The Committee do not accept the reasons of the del ay given by the  Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Financial Services) in the c ase of two notifications that it was due 
to delay in receiving printed copies of notificatio ns. The Committee feels that Ministry did 
not take adequate precaution to avoid the delay. Th e Committee further make a point that 
Ministry should append a delay statement so as to a pprise the Parliament of the reasons of 
delay in laying of notifications on the Table of the House.  
 
(C)  (Department of Revenue) 
 
The Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) hav e laid 127 notifications (Sl. Nos. 
124 -250). Out of these 15 notifications have been delayed. No delay statement is attached with 
any of these delayed notifications. 

  
 The Committee fail to understand why the delay stat ement was not appended to any 
of the notifications while laying on the Table of t he House. While there may be a reason for 
the delay but there can be no reason for not furnis hing the reason for that. The Ministry 
must understand the implication for not doing so re gularly and in such a large number of 
cases. 
 
 The Committee hope that the Ministry of Finance (D epartment of Revenue) would 
take necessary steps to avoid delay in laying of no tifications on the Table of the House in 
future and would append a delay statement in all su ch cases where delay can not be 
avoided. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Departm ent of AYUSH) 
 
  The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Departme nt of AYUSH) have laid 2 
notifications
 (Sl. Nos. 254 & 255) both  of which have a delay pe riod of 6 months to 1 year 
respectively. One notification has no delay statement attached thereto and another notification has 
delay statement appended thereto. The Ministry has cited the reason of procedural matters for not 
laying the notification in time. 
 

 The Committee express anguish that delay was cause d due to procedural matters. 
The Committee are of the opinion that if the Minist ry of Health and Family Welfare 
(Department of AYUSH) deem fit, they should bring n ecessary changes in procedure so as 
to curtail such delays in future. The Committee als o impress upon the Ministry to take note 
of the fact that in case there is a delay in the la ying of any Statutory Notifications, the same 
should be accompanied with a delay statement while it is being laid. The Committee also 
direct  the Ministry to avoid recurrence of such de lays in future and append delay 
statement so as to  keep Parliament apprised of the reasons of delay.  
 
 The Committee also fail to understand how in one c ase delay statement was laid and 
in other case it was not. It is clear case of carel essness on the part of Ministry. The 
Committee feel concerned about such an important is sue not being monitored at the senior 
level and being done as routine work. 
 
(x)      Ministry of Home Affairs  
 
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 20 notificat ions out of which 8 notifications 
have been delayed. The delay period ranges from 3 m onths to 6 months. 6 delayed notifications 
(Sl. Nos. 256-257, 264, 268, 271  & 274) have no de lay statement attached. Only 2 notifications 
are appended with delay statement. The reasons for delayed is as under:-  
 

 “Notification No. G.SR. 789 (E) and S.O. 2687 (E) were required to be laid before both 
the Houses of Parliament while it is in session for  a total period of 30 days as soon as after these 
were made. The Sashastra Seema Bal Combatised, Sub-Inspector (General Duty) Group ‘B’ Non-
Gazetted Posts Recruitment Amendment Rules, 2010 an d provisions of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2008 could not be laid i n the winter session 2010 due to 
adjournment of both the Houses. 
 
 The Committee take serious note of the fact that de lay was caused due to 
adjournment of the House. Ministries should have taken the matter on priority basis so that 
notifications would be laid well before the adjourn ment of the House. This possibility  
should have been assessed well before and adequate arrangements should have been made 
in respect thereof. The Committee advise the Minist ry of Home Affairs to ensure that such 
delays do not recur in future. 
 
(xi) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  
 (Department of Higher Education and Department of School Education and 
Literacy) 
 

The Ministry of Human Resource Development (Departm ent of Higher Education) have 
laid 5 notifications (Sl. Nos. 276-280). Out of the se 4 notifications have been delayed. Delay 
period ranges from 4 months to 1 year and there is no delay statement appended thereto. 
   
  Department of School Education and Literacy have la id 5 notifications (Sl. Nos. 281 – 
285) and all of them have been delayed. The delay p eriod ranges from 7 months to 8 month and 
there is no delay statement appended thereto. The r easons for delay given by the Ministry is as 
under:- 
 
  “These regulations were received on 25.11.2010. H ence, these could not be laid in Winter 
Session of Parliament as there was very little time  left for completion of formalities for laying 
these on the table of both the Houses of Parliament”.  
 
 The Committee observe that sessions are declared mu ch in advance and had the 
Ministry of Human Resource Development  taken promp t steps for laying of the 
notifications, the delay could have been avoided. I t appears to have waited till last moment. 
The Committee, therefore,  recommend that the Minis try should take the first available 
opportunity for laying of their notifications during the session. 
 
(xii) Ministry of Power 
 

 Ministry of Power have laid 6 notifications (Sl. N os. 314 to 319). Out of these one 
notification (Sl. No. 316) has been delayed by 1 ye ar and 2 months and no delay statement is 
attached thereto. Another notification (Sl. No. 314 ) has been delayed by 5 months and 
accompanied with delay statement. The reasons given by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
 “The notification was published in the Gazette of India Extraordinary dated 7 
th  August, 
2010, copies of the notification could not be laid on the Rajya Sabha before conclusion of the 
Monsoon Session 2010 as printed copies of the same were received by Joint Electricity 
Regulatory Commission for Goa and UTs from the Department of Publication, Ministry of Urban 
Development on 6 October, 2010 and Joint Electricit y Regulatory Commission for Goa and UTs 
forwarded the same to Ministry of Power on 6 th  October, 2010. The Monsoon Session concluded 
on 27 th  August, 2010. Hence the notification is laid on the first opportunity.” 
  
 This is just not acceptable to the Committee that 5 out 6 notifications laid by the 
Ministry did not have delay statements. While there may be a reason for the delay but there 
can be no reason for not furnishing reason for that . The Ministry must understand the 
implications for not doing so regularly and in such a large number of cases. 
 
 The Committee do not accept the reasons of the del ay given by the  Ministry of 
Power in the case of two notifications that it was due to delay in receiving printed copies of 
notifications. The Committee feel that Ministry did  not take adequate precaution to avoid 

the delay. The Committee further make a point that Ministry should append a delay 
statement so as to apprise the Parliament of the reasons of delay in laying of notifications on 
the Table of the House. 
 
 
 
(xiii)     Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have laid  24 notifications
 on the Table of 
the House (Sl. Nos. 320 to 343). 9 notifications ha ve been delayed out of which 5 notifications 
accompanied with delay statements and 4 notificatio ns have no delay statements appended to 
them. The delay period ranges from 3 months to 8 mo nths. The reasons given by the Ministry is 
that it took some time to complete the procedural f ormalities and therefore, papers could not be 
laid in time. 
 
 The Committee are anguished to see that  the Minist ry of Road Transport & 
Highways not only had delayed the laying of 9 of it s notification, it had also failed to lay 
delay statement and it is required to do so. The Co mmittee in this connection invite 
attention to its recommendation contained in its 13 5 
th  Report. The Committee have decided 
to take a serious view in such failures particularl y by a Ministry like Road Transport & 
Highways that lays fairly large number of notificat ions etc. during every session. The 

Ministry should know that such failure in laying pa pers amounts to curtailing the 
Parliament’s right to be informed about subordinate legislations.  
 
(xiv) Ministry of Science and Technology 
 
 (Department of Science and Technology) 
  
 The Committee note with regret that the Ministry of Science and Technology (Department 
of Science and Technology) have delayed the laying of their only notification (Sl. No. 344) by 8 
months and  no delay statement appended with the said notifications. 
 
The Ministry must be aware of the Committee’s recom mendations in its 135 Report 
that in case of delay in laying, notifications shou ld be accompanied with delay statement. 
The Ministry should appreciate the constitutional significance behind that requirement that  
flows from the principle of parliamentary control o f subordinate legislations. It therefore, 
should take care that repetition of such delay is avoided in future. 
 
(xv) Ministry of Textiles 
 
Ministry of Textiles has laid only  one notificatio n  and that has no delay statement 
appended thereto. The delay period is of 6 months. 

 
 The Committee take a serious view not only about t he delay in laying of one of its 
notification on the Table of the House but also failure to append the delay statement with it. 
The Ministry/Department must know about the possibl e implications of failing to meet this 
requirement. It must ensure to append a delay statement in all cases in future. 
 
(xvi) Ministry of Urban Development 
 
 Only one notification (Sl. No. 350) that Ministry o f Urban Development have laid is 
delayed by 6 months and delay statement  is appended thereto. The reasons for delay given by the 
Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “Gazette Notification of Delhi Metro Airport Expre ss Line, General Rules, 2010 was 
notified in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Pa rt II  Section-III sub-section (i) on 19.09.2010 
and same was processed on 16.11.2010. The scrutiny and processing of the Notification for 
laying on the Table of the Lok Sabha and Rajya  Sab ha could not be completed within the Winter 
Session of Parliament, which concluded on 13.12.2010 because there were other pressing matters 
required to be dealt within a time bound manner.” 
 
 The Committee express deep concern and take excepti on for taking contemptuous 
stand and treating the laying of notification on th e Table of the House as a matter of 

subsidiary importance. Other matters were given pre ference over this matter which is a 
constitutional obligation. The Committee have decid ed to seek explanation from the 
Ministry regarding this issue. 
 
The Committee time and again have emphasized that l aying of 
rules/regulations/orders is a statutory obligation and should be completed on priority basis 
within specified time-frame. The Ministry of Urban Development should understand the 
implication of such failures. However, the Ministry  of Urban Development have not 
complied with the recommendations of the Committee in this regard. The Committee once 
again emphasise that Ministry of Urban Development should adhere to the time schedule in 
laying of notifications as prescribed in Committee’s 131 
st  Report. 
  
3. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/ Departments to take immediate steps to 
ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legi slation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes 
to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Department s of the Government of India, particularly, the 
defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st 
,135 
th  and 152 nd  
Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in 

the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Se ssion, on the date of the publication of the 
Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than  15 clear days, before the expiry of the 
Session immediately following the said Session. All  the Ministries/Departments of 
Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of 
the Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is 
a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the conc erned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to 
take a note of this, since the intension is that th rough the process of formulation of a delay 
statement the Ministry is able to introspect, ident ify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 

(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/Departments 
should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished 
from one another. 
(152 
nd 
 Report)

INTRODUCTION 
 
1. I, the Chairperson of the Committee on Subordina te Legislation, having been authorized 
by the Committee, do hereby present on its behalf, this One Hundred and Ninety Sixth Report of 
the Committee.  
 
2.  The Committee examined the matters that came up    while   scrutinizing (i) The Tea 
(Marketing) Control Order, 2003 and (ii) the Prohib ition on Sale of Cigarettes and other     
Tobacco Products around Educational Institutions Ru les, 2004 and issues relating to them along 
with the comments received from the concerned Governments. 
 
3.   The observations and recommendations of the Co mmittee are contained in the Report.  
 
4. The Committee considered and adopted the draft R eport in its meeting held on the 14 
th  
December, 2011

Report 
I 
The Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003 
 The Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003 ( Annexure I ) framed under the Tea Act, 1953 
were taken up for examination by the Committee on S ubordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha.  The 
Committee had earlier examined the Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 1984 and the matter was 
reported to the House vide the 127 th  Report of the Committee presented to the House on the 14 th  
March, 2000. The Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 200 3 has been framed by the Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce) in s upersession of the Order of 1984. The 
Order of 1984 had been examined in detail by the Co mmittee and all its suggestions relating to 
the provision of the Order have since been carried out by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
vide the Tea (Marketing) Control (Amendment) Order, 1999.  
 
2. However, a perusal of the Tea (Marketing) Order,  2003 revealed that it did not 
incorporate some of the amendments which had been c arried out through the Amendment Order 
of 1999 on the basis of the recommendations of the Committee. These included 
recommendations of the Committee on paragraphs 21 a nd 23 of the 1984 Order. Vide 
Amendment Order of 1999, in paragraphs 23 of the 19 84 Order, after the words “or any officer 
of the Board”, the words “not below the rank of ins pector” were inserted but in paragraph 27 of 
the Order of 2003, the words “not below the rank of  inspector” are missing. Similarly, while the 
Committee was considering the Order of 1984, the Go vernment had agreed to delete the 
provisions of paragraph 21 of the Order of 1984 reg arding Constitution of the Committee on Tea 
Marketing. But the provision finds place vide 
 paragraph 25 of the Order of 2003. Accordingly, a 
reference was made to the Ministry of Commerce & In dustry (Department of Commerce) on the 
16 th  July, 2004 seeking clarifications on these discrep ancies apart from some general questions 
on the Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003. The poi nts referred to the Ministry and the 
comments/clarifications received thereon are place at Annexure-II . 
 

3. The Committee also took up the matter for discus sion with the representatives of the Tea 
Board and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry at Kolkata on the 25 th  October, 2004. 
Relevant extracts from the study note ( Annexure III ) on the above discussion was forwarded to 
the Ministry for necessary action on the 31 st  March, 2005. The Ministry vide  their 
communication dated the 20 th  July, 2005 have since furnished Action Taken Note. A summary of 
the points referred to the Ministry and the action taken by them are given below: 
 
3.1  Regarding the need of supersession of the Order of 1984 by a new one, the Committee 
was informed that the depressed condition of the te a industry in the country since the end of 
1999 had given rise to the need for more accurate i nformation in order to facilitate effective 
decisions. Accordingly, a number of changes were re quired to be made in the Order of 1984 and 
a new Order of 2003 was brought into effect. The Co mmittee took note of the changes brought 
out in the new order.  
  
3.2 It was pointed out by the Committee that the Mi nistry had not been careful enough to 
take note of its earlier recommendations contained in its 127 
th  Report while formulating the 
Order of 2003. The Committee was informed that para graph 25 of Tea (Marketing) Control 
Order, 2003 has been deleted vide Notification S.O. 1170(E), dated the 20 th  October, 2004 
regarding the Tea (Marketing) Control (Second Amendment) Order, 2004 
 
3.3  The Committee found that the Ministry did not take note of its recommendations 
contained in its 127 
th  Report to include the words “not below the rank of  Inspector” in the 
corresponding paragraph 27 of the new Order. The Co mmittee, however, noted that the Ministry 
had since done the same through an amendment Notification  
 
3.4  The Committee noted that the Order of 2003 prescrib ed a stricter regulation for auctions, 
marketing activities and the calling for informatio n from the persons engaged in this industry. 

The committee wondered how such regulatory activiti es could be welcomed in the current era of 
autonomy and liberalization. The Committee felt tha t the objectives of the Order did not warrant 
prescription of such high levels of regulation. The  fact that the Tobacco Board was also 
monitoring the primary marketing of tobacco was not justified in the Committee’s opinion. 
 The Ministry informed the Committee that in order to bring greater transparency in the 
primary marketing of tea and for effective data col lection and collation, it was necessary to 
incorporate a provision in the Tea (Marketing) Cont rol Order enabling registration of one of the 
important stakeholders of tea industry viz. primary  buyers of tea. Further, in order to protect the 
consumers from supply of any adulterated tea, a pro vision was incorporated stipulating that the 
tea should conform to the specifications as laid do wn under the prevention of Food Adulteration 
Act, 1954 as amended from time to time or any other  rules for the time being in force. A 
provision has also been incorporated for fixation o f a price sharing formula so as to ensure that 
the small tea growers get a reasonable share of the  price obtained by the manufacturer of made 
tea. Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003 also has a n enabling provision empowering the Tea 
Board to issue directives to the Auction Organizers , Brokers etc. for improving the efficiency of 
the present auctioning system, so as to reduce the cost and time in selling tea through auction and 
also to enable the auction system to handle more volume of tea. 
 
3.5   The Committee felt that the scheme of the Order ves ted most of the powers with the 
Chairman of the Board. The Committee, accordingly, desired that the Ministry/ Tea Board re-
examine this point. The Ministry informed the Commi ttee that the matter has already been 
examined. Under the new Tea (Marketing) Control Ord er, 2003, powers have been vested with 
the Chairman of the Tea Board with a view to implem ent various provisions of the Order 
effectively. The implementation of the different pr ovisions of the Order is being made with the 
assistance of the Tea Board’s officials located in different parts of India. Moreover, any 
directives which are required to be issued by the C hairman, Tea Board, are based on the 
recommendations of experts and taking into account the views obtained from different 
stakeholders of the tea industry. Under the new Ord er, the Chairman is also required to consult 
the Department in all important policy matters. 

 
3.6  To a query raised by the Committee on the constitution of a Committee on Tea Marketing 
under paragraph 25 of the 2003 Order, the Ministry informed that so far no Committee had been 
constituted under paragraph 25 of the Order of 2003 .  Instead, paragraph 25 of Tea (Marketing) 
Control Order, 2003 had been deleted vide 
 Notification S.O. 1170(E) dated the 20 October, 
2004, publishing the Tea (Marketing) Control (Second Amendment) Order, 2004. 
 
3.7 The Members enquired about the status of tea in dustry in the North-Eastern region. They 
also showed concern regarding changing trend in the  tea industry and impressed upon the 
Ministry/ Tea Board to take necessary steps to inte rcept and prevent the closing of tea gardens. 
The Committee observed that the points raised by th e Members were noted by the 
representatives of the Tea Board for taking appropriate action. 
 The Committee was informed that the Indian tea ind ustry has been passing through a 
period of depressed prices during the last few year s. The continuous fall in prices of tea, high 
costs of production, fall in exports etc. have adve rsely affected the viability of tea gardens, 
particularly the medium sized and financially weak ones, resulting in closure/abandonment of 
some tea gardens in the country. The industry is al so faced with long term problems like old age 
of the plantations, worn-out machinery in the proce ssing factories and poor infrastructure 
facilities. 
During the last few years, 118 tea gardens were clo sed in different parts of the country. 
However, 86 tea gardens have been re-opened while t he number of tea gardens that remain 
closed at present is 27. Also, the Central Governme nt and the Tea Board have facilitated 
discussions on the matter between the managements of the closed tea gardens and their bankers.  
 
4. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Commerc e and Industry have since 
amended the Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003 as per its recommendations and 
notified the same as follows: 

(i) The Ministry vide  its Notification No. S.O. 270 (E) dated the 27 th  February, 2004 
(Annexure-IV) have published the Tea (Marketing) Co ntrol (Amendment) Order, 2004 
wherein necessary amendment has been made by way of  insertion of the words ‘not below 
the rank of Assistant Development Officer or Inspec tor’ after the words ‘any officer of the 
Board’ for the purpose of search and seizure; and 
 
(ii) The Ministry vide 
 its Notification No. S.O. 1170 (E) dated the 20 th  October, 2004 
(Annexure- V) have published the Tea (Marketing) Co ntrol (Second Amendment) Order, 
2004 where by Para 25 of the Order of 2003 which em powered Central Government to 
constitute a Committee on tea marketing has been deleted. 
5. The Committee notes that  the Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 1984 were replaced 
by the Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003, which prescribes for stricter regulation of the 
auctions, marketing activities and the calling for information from the persons engaged in 
this industry.  The Committee, however, feels that the objectives o f the Order did not 
warrant prescription of such high levels of regulat ion in the current era of autonomy and 
liberalization. The fact that the Tobacco Board is also monitoring the primary marketing 
of tobacco is no justification in the Committee’s o pinion.  The Committee, further, observes 
that certain provisions of the 2003 Order reportedl y caused some concern to the buyer 
community with regard to their implementation espec ially the provisions relating to 
definition of buyer/manufacturer, his registration, payment for registration fee, submission 
of returns etc.  The Committee notes that in  order to remove the genuine difficulties of the 
various sections of the tea industry for the purpos e of implementation and compliance of 
the new order, the Government has since brought ame ndments to the Tea (Marketing) 
Control Order 2003 by way of Tea (Marketing) Contro l (Amendment) Order, 2004 .  It is 
hoped that the amendments to Tea (Marketing) Contro l Order 2003 will help in removing 
the genuine difficulties faced by the buyers/sellers of tea. 
   
 

II 
The Prohibition on Sale of Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products around Educational 
Institutions Rules, 2004 
 
 The Prohibition on Sale of Cigarettes and other To bacco Products around Educational 
Institutions Rules, 2004 (Annexure I)  have been framed under the Cigarettes and other To bacco 
Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulati on of Trade and Commerce, Production, 
Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003.  The Rules proh ibit sale of cigarettes and other tobacco 
products within a radius of one hundred yards of th e educational institutions and the offence is 
punishable with a fine which may extend to two hund red rupees.  Since the teenagers and young 
school/ college going students are most vulnerable group to the addiction of tobacco, this 
provision (to ban the sale of tobacco products 100 yards around educational institutions) was 
made. The Prohibition on Sale of Cigarettes and oth er Tobacco Products around Educational 
Institutions Rules, 2004 was notified in the Gazett e of India vide G.S.R. 561 (E) dated 1 st  
September, 2004.  The Rules were laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha on the 30 th  August, 
2005.  
2. The Committee took up for examination the said r ules and a questionnaire on the subject 
matter was forwarded to the Ministry of Health & Fa mily Welfare (Department of Health) for 
their comments/ clarifications on the 10 
th  July, 2006.  The Ministry furnished their comments / 
clarifications on the 2 nd  November, 2006 (Annexure II).   A summary of the points raised by the 
Committee and the comments of the Ministry received  thereon have been summerized in the 
succeeding paragraphs:  
3. The Committee pointed to the delay of 11 months from the notification of the Prohibition 
on Sale of Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products ar ound Educational Institutions Rules, 2004 to 
its laying before Parliament.  The Ministry attribu ted this delay to the late receipt of the required 
number of copies of printed notification from the G overnment of India Press; hence it could not 
be laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament in time.   
4. On the point relating to the boards to be displa yed by the manager/person in-charge of an 
educational institution, the Ministry stated that t he rules provide the board to be displayed at a 

conspicuous place outside the educational premises stating prominently that sale is prohibited 
within a radius of one hundred yards, and that ther e should not be any objection from the 
educational institutions in prominently displaying the board.   
5. On the Committee’s view that the fine of Rs. 200 /- for not displaying such a board was 
too  low and that the same should be increased so t hat it acts as a deterrent, the Ministry 
informed that they did not have any objection to en hancing the penalty and that the Ministry 
would consider the same as and when a comprehensive  amendment of the Tobacco Act, 2003 is 
taken up.   
6. On the use of imperial system of measurement of distance (of 11 yards from educational 
institutions) rather than the metric system which i s more prevalent, the Ministry stated that the 
distance of 100 yards has been specified in the Act .  The Ministry, however, submitted that they 
did not have any objection in replacing the ‘yards’  with ‘Meters, whenever amendment to the 
Act would be taken up.  
7. Thereafter, Committee heard the Secretary, Minis try of Health and Family Welfare 
(Department of Health) on the 8 th  January, 2010.  During the course of discussion, t he 
Committee raised the issues relating to increasing use of cigarettes and tobacco products 
amongst youngsters, process of monitoring of implem entation of the rules, periodic assessment 
of target fixed and achieved and sufficiency of qua ntum of fine/ penalty.  The Committee was 
informed that the growing use of tobacco products a mongst youngsters was basically due to peer 
pressure.  It was therefore, important to educate t he children from tender age about the damages 
caused-social, economical, physical, etc. by the us e of cigarettes and other tobacco products.   
The Ministry also informed the Committee that they had earmarked almost Rs. 50 crores for 
media campaigns to educate and create awareness in this regard .  While the reality of the huge 
agricultural labourers and farmers dependent on its  production was a fact that cannot be ignored, 
a conscious decision had been taken by the Ministry  to provide alternative cropping system to 
the farmers producing tobacco. The Committee was as sured that the punishment prescribed 
under the Act and the Rules are sufficient enough.   
8. The concerns expressed and queries raised by the  Members during the meeting was 
forwarded to the Ministry of Health & Family Welfar e vide  this Secretariat letter dated 3 rd  

February, 2010 as contained in the verbatim oral ev idence sent with a request to furnish 
information/replies to the  Committee.  Another letter was sent to the Ministry on the 30 th  March, 
2010, for expediting the replies.  But to the Commi ttee’s surprise, the Ministry did not furnish 
the replies.         
 
General Observations/ Recommendations of the Committee 
 
9. The Committee observes that tobacco product manu facturers increasingly focus on 
youth and children.  Our efforts, therefore, should  be to ensure that tobacco products are 
not easily available to children and that they are prevented from involuntary smoke as 
enshrined in the Preamble to the Act.   The Committ ee, accordingly, hopes that the 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare would conscio usly and diligently work towards this 
end so that the  Rules serve the purpose of the law in true spirit a part from complying with 
our Treaty obligations under Framework Convention o n Tobacco Control (FCTC).  We 
ought to adopt all the  international best practice s in implementing the law in letter and 
spirit.   
10. The Committee expresses its concern that childr en between the age group of 13-15 
years are taking to smoking.  The Ministry’s attemp t for detoxification and to get the 
youngsters de-addicted from tobacco has not been ve ry successful.  The Committee notes 
that the Ministry is taking action for strict imple mentation of the rules under the Code of 
Criminal Procedure (Cr. P.C.).  The Committee, however, feels that much more needs to be 
done to bring about the required behavioural change  amongst youth and school going 
children by starting aggressive education and aware ness programmes through media 
campaigns.  The Committee noticed that after the me eting, a visible media campaign 
depicting dangerous effects of using tobacco products was started and warnings/pictures on 
cigarettes and chewing tobacco was made more promin ent.  It had no doubt had the 
desired impact.  The Committee compliments the agen cies-government and non-
government involved in this and calls upon them to continue this effort with renewed 
vigour. 

11. The Committee deprecates the laxity shown by th e Ministry in laying the 
notification on the Table of the House.  The Commit tee is not convinced by the reason 
advanced (non-availability of printed copies of the  notification) and feels that the time of 
one year in procuring the printed copies was not at  all acceptable. The Committee does not 
approve of such inordinate delay in laying the pape rs and directs that such delays should 
not recur in future. The Ministry must evolve suita ble arrangements with the Ministry of 
Urban Development to avoid delays in preparing prin ted copies from Government of India 
Press in future. 
12. The Committee notes that the Ministry have no o bjection in replacing the imperial 
system of measurement of distance of hundred yards as specified in the Act by the metric 
system which is more prevalent today and which woul d require amendment to the Act.  
The Committee hopes the Ministry would do that as a nd when amendment of the Tobacco 
Act, 2003 is considered. 
13. The rules provide that the display board should  be displayed at a conspicuous place 
outside the educational premises stating prominently that sale is prohibited within a radius 
of one hundred yards and that there should not be a ny objection from the educational 
institutions in prominently displaying the board.   The Committee, accordingly, 
recommends the Ministry to ensure that this rule is  strictly adhered to and the display 
boards are prominently displayed and directs the Mi nistry of Health & Family Welfare to 
furnish a status report on the number of educationa l institutions in Delhi and NCR 
(National Capital Region) which are not complying w ith this rule.  Regular inspections 
should be done in this regard. 
14. The Committee is aware that peer pressure was t he single factor for youngsters to 
take to smoking. The tobacco companies also, theref ore, consciously work on the young 
people for two reasons.  One, peer pressure is easier to build and two, it is fashionable.  The 
Committee is concerned over the serious health haza rds including high health costs of the 
treatment of cancer and cardiovascular diseases, of which 30% are cancer cases on account 
of tobacco.  The Committee is happy that the Minist ry has undertaken the “Global Adult 
Tobacco Survey and hopes that the Ministry would co nsciously and consistently work 

towards taking steps for effective monitoring and a ssessment at every stage of the 
implementation of the rules.   
15. The Committee found that the monitoring of impl ementation of Rules left much to 
be desired.  One can find shops and vendors selling  tobacco products within the prohibited 
area of 100 yards from school/ educational institut ional premises.  The Committee feels 
that strict vigilance around the educational instit utions was required. The Committee 
observes that punishment for violations or non obse rvance of Rule has to be quick and 
significant,  if it is to act as a deterrent. Then only, can the menace of tobacco be contained.  
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Health & F amily Welfare does not have any 
objection and has assured to enhance the penalty fo r selling tobacco products within 100 
yards from educational institutions from the existi ng Rs 200/- as and when a 
comprehensive amendment of the Tobacco Act, 2003 could be considered. 
16. The Committee is happy to note that an attempt has been made by the Ministry of 
Health and Family Welfare to provide alternative cr opping system and alternative 
livelihood to the tobacco growers/farmers and the p eople working in tobacco industries 
who will be displaced.  The Committee appreciates t he Ministry’s efforts to select some 
vocations which can be beneficial for the small sho pkeepers who are dependent for their 
livelihood on the sale of tobacco products.  The Co mmittee hopes that the Ministries of 
Health and Family Welfare, Labour, Rural Developmen t, Industry and Commerce would 
coordinate with each other to find a workable solut ion in this regard to everyone’s 
satisfaction 
 
17. The Committee takes a serious view of the Minis try not furnishing information/ 
replies on the concerns and queries raised by the M embers of the Committee during it’s 
meeting despite two letters sent by the Committee S ecretariat in this regard.  The 
Committee, therefore, takes this opportunity to giv e specific directions in the matter so as 
to ensure prompt disposal of its references made to  the 
Ministries/Departments/Organizations etc.  The repl ies should be furnished positively 
within a month and in case it is not possible to do  so within one month of the receipt of the 

reference in the Ministry, the Committee may be inf ormed of the reasons of delay in 
writing and specific request be made to the Committee for the extension of time.

3. The Committee considered the draft 195 th  Report  on Statutory Orders Laid on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha during its 222 nd  Session and noticed inordinate delays in the framing as well as laying of 
rules, regulations, etc. by the different Ministries/ Departments.  The Committee found that the 
Ministries/ Departments were not following strictly the Committee’s recommendations contained in its 
127 th  Report in this regard and that the time limits were also not being adhered to by them for 
framing/laying of various subordinate legislations. Apart from delay in laying/framing these instruments, 
the mandatory Delay Statements giving reason for delay were also not being submitted in large number 
of the cases. The Committee expressed concern over the Ministries/Departments not following its 
recommendation/observation made in such matters in its reports submitted after every session. The 
manner in which such an important matter is being handled by the Ministries/Departments is, no doubt, 
causal and it appears that no senior officers were supervising this activity. This attitude has been noticed 
not only in one or two but with most of the Ministries/Departments.  
4. The Committee felt that delaying paper to be laid on Table of the House or not doing so in 
required form was tantamount to showing disregard to its recommendation and well laid out 
procedures. The Committee  strongly feels that the Ministries/Departments need to be sensitized about 
this and calls upon the Cabinet Secretary  and the Secretary,  Department of Parliamentary Affairs to 
play a proactive  role for ensuring that Subordinate Legislation were not only framed in time but also 
brought before the House strictly as per the laid out procedure and time frame.

2. During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee noted 
some cases where there has been a considerable time  lag between the date of 
notification of the Order and the date of its layin g. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where notifi cations have not been laid as 
per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and wh ere such notifications 
were not accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in 
laying. In some of the cases, the delay has been qu ite long. The 
observations/recommendations of the Committee in re spect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Agriculture 
 (Department of Agriculture and Cooperation) 
 
Out of 10 notifications (Sl. Nos. 1 to 10) laid by the Ministry of Agriculture 
(Department of Agriculture and Cooperation),  2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 2 and 
5)  have  been delayed by four months and 6 months respectively. There is  no 
delay statements appended to any of them  
 
The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the de lay in laying 
of Notifications. Moreover, there is no delay state ment attached thereto. 
The Committee reiterates its recommendation contain ed in its 135 
th  
Report that in case of delay in laying, Notificatio ns should invariably be 

 
accompanied with delay statement. The Ministry shou ld take care that 
repetition of such delay is avoided in future. 
 
(ii) Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers  
 (Department of Fertilizers) 
 
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department o f Fertilizers) have 
laid 4 Notifications (Sl.No.11 to 14), two of which  (Sl. No. 11 & 12)  have 
been delayed by 9 months and 8 months respectively.  There is no delay 
statement appended to any of these. 
 
The Committee regrets the delay in laying of Notifi cations by the 
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department o f Fertilizers) and 
emphasises that the Ministry should strictly adhere to the time schedule as 
recommended by it in its 131 
st  Report  in laying of the Subordinate 
Legislation before Parliament and in case of any de lay in laying of the 
notifications, a delay statement should also invariably be appended. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Civil Aviation 
 
Ministry of Civil Aviation have laid 6 Notification s (Sl.Nos.15-20), out 
of these only one Notification (Sl.No.15) has been delayed by 1 year. There is 
no delay statement appended thereto. 
 
The Committee expresses its concern over the inordinate delay that 
has taken place in the laying of the one Notificati on. The Committee  also 
takes serious note of the fact that the Ministry has not appended any delay 
statement with the delayed Notification.  In absenc e of any delay 
statement Committee is not in a position to ascerta in what caused this 
inordinate delay. The Committee, therefore,  recomm ends that the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation should take all necessar y precaution in future 
so as to avoid recurrence of such situations and ap pend delay statements 
where required. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Commerce and  Industry 
(Department of Commerce and Department of Industria l Policy 
and Promotion) 
 
 Ministry of  Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce and  
Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion) have  laid 11 (Sl. Nos. 21 to 
31)  Notifications, out of which Department of Comm erce have laid 7 
Notifications and Department of Industrial Policy a nd Promotion have laid 4 
Notifications. 7 Notifications (Department of Comme rce(Sl. Nos. 21, 23-25) 
and  Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion [Sl. Nos. 28-30]) have 
been delayed and delay period ranges from 4 months to 11 months. There is no 
delay statement appended to any of these delayed Notifications. 

 
 
The Committee is concerned to see that  the Ministr y of Commerce 
and Industry has failed to lay delay statement that   is a statutory 
requirement. The Committee in this connection invit es attention to its 
recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report. The Committee takes a 
serious view in such failures. The Ministry should know that failure to lay 
papers amounts to curtailing Parliament’s right to be informed about 
subordinate legislations. 
 
(v) Ministry of Communications and Information Tech nology 
(a) (Department of Posts) 
  
Ministry of Communications and Information Technolo gy (Department 
of Posts) have laid 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 32 to  36) . Out of these  one  
Notification ( Sl. No. 36) have been delayed by 6 m onths. There is no delay 
statement appended thereto. 
 
The Committee takes a serious view not only about t he delay in 
laying of one of its Notifications on the Table of the House but also failure 
to append the delay statement with them. The Minist ry/Department must 
know about the possible implications of failing to meet this requirement. It 
must ensure to append a delay statement in all such cases in future . 
 
  (b)   (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
 Ministry of Communications and Information Technol ogy (Department 
of Telecommunications) have laid 7 Notifications (S l. Nos. 37 to 43). All of 
these have been delayed by 5 months to 9 months. Th ere is no delay statement 
appended to four (Sl. Nos. 40-43) of these. Only 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 37-
39) have delay statement appended to them. The reas ons of delay given by the 
Department of Telecommunications is given as under:- 
 
 “The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is a statutory 
body set up under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997. In 
exercise of the powers conferred upon it under sect ion 36 of the TRAI Act, 
1997, the Authority may, by notification, make regu lations consistent with the 
Act and the Rules made there under to carry out the purposes of the Act. Under 
section 37 of the Act, the regulations notified by TRAI are required to be laid 
before each House of Parliament. 
 The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) i n exercise of the 
powers conferred by section 36, read with sub-claus es (v) of clause (b) of sub-
section (1) and clause (c) of sub-section (1) of se ction 11 of the TRAI Act, 
1997 notified “The Telecom Commercial Communication s customer 
Preference (Second Amendment Regulations, 2010.”Thi s Regulation was 
issued to amend the main regulation titled “The Tel ecom Commercial 
Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 201 0 (6 of 2010) dated 1 
st  

 
December 2010.” Main Regulation was given for printing to government press. 
However, before receipt of printed copies of the ma in regulation from 
Government Press on 21 
st  January, 2011, two amendments to the regulations 
(including this regulation) has been issued. Circum stances have changed in 
such a manner that effective date of implementation  of the regulations has to 
be changed from time to time for reasons beyond the control of TRAI. Till date 
five amendments to regulations have been issued. Fi fth Amendment to 
regulations has been issued on 18 th  March, 2011. In order to provide holistic 
and accurate information on the subject and to avoi d confusion by providing 
piece meal information to the Hon’ble Members of th e House while laying the 
copies of regulations in both houses of Parliament,  TRAI sent all the 
regulations to DoT on 7 th  April, 2011. Accordingly, the regulations are bein g 
laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” 
  
The Committee is not convinced by the reason given by the 
Ministry that the Notification could not be laid do wn because there were 
amendments to the Regulation taking place in the me antime. The 
Committee is of the strong view that Ministry shoul d have given priority 
to lay the main Regulation on the Table of the Hous e and amendments 
would have been tabled thereafter. 
As it is constitutional provision to lay the Notifi cation within a 
prescribed time-schedule, the Ministry should have taken appropriate 
action to lay the same on the Table of the House. T he Committee, 
therefore, recommends that adequate precaution shou ld be exercised to 
avoid recurrence of such instances in future. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
  
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs  (Department of Consu mer Affairs and 
Department of Food and Public Distribution) have la id 16 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 44 to 59). Department of Consumer Affairs have  laid 9 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 44 to 52) and Department of Food and Public Di stribution  have laid 7

   The Committee notes that there has been not only de lay in the 
laying of Notifications, but no delay statement has  been attached thereto. 
The Committee views it seriously as it defies recommendation contained in 
its 135 
th  Report that in case of delay in laying, Notificati ons should 
invariably be accompanied with a delay statement. T he Ministry should 
take care that repetition of such defiance is avoided in future.  
 
 
 

 
(vii) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 49 notific ations (Sl. Nos. 60 to 
108) out of which 21 Notifications have been delaye d by 4 months to 9 
months.  There is no delay statement  appended to a ny of these delayed

 The Committee is not happy over the delay in layin g of the

therefore, impresses upon  the Ministry to  devise suitable mechanism to

th  Report.  
 
(viii)  Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 
 Ministry of Environment and Forests have laid 24 N otifications (Sl.

each of seriousness in the Ministry in fulfilling i ts constitutional 
responsibility to Parliament. 
 
 
(ix)  Ministry of Finance 
  
(a)    (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs ) have laid 19

laying of twenty five Notifications (by the Department of Economic Affairs

its failure to append the required delay statement.  The 
Ministry/Department must know about the possible im plications of failing 
to meet this requirement that tantamounts to diluti ng Executive’s

 (c)   (Department of Revenue) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) have la id 146 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 181 to 326). Out of these 5 2 Notifications have been

This is just not acceptable to the Committee that 5 2 out of 146

(x) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
           (Department of Health) 
 
  The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare ( Departm ent of Health) 
have laid 6 Notifications
 (Sl. Nos. 327 to 332) out of which 2 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 328 and 329) have been delayed. There is delay   of 5 to 6 months. There

fact that in case there is a delay in the laying of  any Statutory 
Notifications, the same should be accompanied with a delay statement 
while it is being laid. The Committee also directs  the Ministry to avoid 
recurrence of such delays in future and append dela y statement so as to  
keep Parliament apprised of the reasons of delay.

The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 45 Notificat ions (Sl. Nos.

impresses upon the Ministry to take note of the fac t that in case there is a 
delay in the laying of any Statutory Notifications,  the same should be 
accompanied by a delay statement while it is being laid . The Committee 
also advises the Ministry to avoid recurrence of such delays in future. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
(xvi) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas have laid  4 Notifications 
(Sl. Nos. 417-420). All of these Notifications have  been delayed. The delay 
period ranges from 4 to 10 months. There is no dela y statement appended to 
any of them. 
 
The Committee takes strong exception to the Ministr y’s failure to 
lay the delay statement. The Committee in the absen ce of delay statements 
are not able to know the reasons behind this delay.  Therefore, the 
Committee invites attention to its recommendation c ontained in its 135
th  
Report  in this connection where it is observed to append invariably delay 
statement in case of delay in laying of notificatio ns by  the Ministry. The 
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should also e ndeavour to avoid 
recurrence of such delays in future. 
 
(xvii) Ministry of Power 
 
The Ministry of Power have laid 10 Notifications (S l. Nos. 421-430). 
Out of these 6 Notifications have been delayed. The  delay period ranges from 
5 to 16 months. There is no delay statement attached to five of the notifications 
delayed. Only one Notification has delay statement attached to it. The reasons 
of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“Although the above Notification was published in t he Gazette of India 
Extraordinary dated 14 
th  February, 2011, copies of the notification could not be 
laid on table of the Rajya Sabha before conclusion of the Budget Session 2010 
as printed copies of the same were received by Cent ral Electricity Authority 
from the Department of Publication, Ministry of Urb an Development on 28 th  
March, 2011 and CEA forwarded the same to Ministry of Power on 28 th  
March, 2011. The Budget Session concluded on 25 th  March, 2011. Hence the 
notification is laid on the first opportunity.” 
 
The Committee is not inclined to accept the late re ceipt of printed 
copies from the Government of India Press as a vali d reason for a delayed 
laying of Notifications etc. The Ministry of Power  should in future ensure 
that all its papers were laid before the House as p rescribed in the 
Committee’s 131 
st  Report. The Ministry should also append delay 
statement where delay in laying of Notifications on  the Table of the House 
has occurred. The Committee in this connection invi tes attention to its 
recommendations contained in its 135 th  Report.  
 
(xviii) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have la id 180 
notifications (Sl. Nos. 433-612). Out of these 149 Notifications have been 

 
delayed. 16 Notifications are attached with delay s tatement and 133 
Notifications have no delay statement appended. The  delay period ranges from 
5 to 16 months. The reasons given by the Ministry i s that it took some time to 
collect the papers and complete the procedural form alities and therefore, 
notifications could not be laid on time. 
 
This is just not acceptable to the Committee that 1 33 out of 180 
Notifications laid by the Ministry did not have del ay statements. While 
there may be a reason for the delay, but there cann ot be any reason for 
not furnishing reason for that. The Ministry must u nderstand the 
implications for not doing so regularly and in such  a large number of 
cases. 
 
Moreover the Committee do not accept the reasons of  the delay 
given by the  Ministry of Road Transport and Highwa ys that it was due to 
delay in receiving printed copies of Notifications.  How can it take one to 
two years to receive Notifications after printing. The Committee feels that 
Ministry did not take adequate precaution to avoid the delay. The 
Committee further makes a point that Ministry shoul d append a delay 
statement so as to apprise the Parliament of the re asons of delay in laying 
of Notifications on the Table of the House.  
 
(xix) Ministry of Shipping  
  Ministry of Shipping have laid 5 Notifications (S l. Nos. 615 to 619). 
Two of these (Sl. Nos. 615 and 616) have been delay ed by 4 months to 6 
months and no delay statement is appended thereto. 
  The Committee is not happy with the delay in laying  of 
Notifications by the Ministry of Shipping. The Comm ittee desires that the 
Ministry of Shipping append delay statements where there is delay in 
laying of Notifications and avoid recurrence of such delay in future. 
(xx)  Ministry of Textiles 
 The only Notification (Sl. No. 621) that the Minis try of Textiles have 
laid is delayed by 5 months and no delay statement is  appended to it. 
  
 The Ministry must be aware of the Committee’s recom mendations 
in its 135 Report that in case of delay in laying, Notifications should be 
accompanied with delay statement. The Ministry shou ld appreciate the 
constitutional significance behind that requirement  that  flows from the 
principle of parliamentary control of subordinate legislations. It therefore, 
should take care that repetition of such delay is avoided in future. 
 
 
 

 
(xxi) Ministry of Urban Development 
 Only one Notification (Sl. No. 622) that Ministry of Urban 
Development have laid is delayed by 6 months with d elay statement appended 
thereto. The reasons for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “Copies of the Delhi Urban Art Commission (Terms a nd Conditions of 
Service) (Amendment) Rules. 2011 which was publishe d in the Gazette of 
India, Part II  Section 3 (i) dated 22.1.2011were r equired to be laid on the 
Table of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha in the Budget Sessio n 2011. The same could 
not be sent in time since the duration of Budget Session 2011 was curtailed and 
the session concluded on 25.3.2011. 
 
Delay caused in laying the Delhi Urban Art Commissi on (Terms and 
Conditions of Service) (Amendment) Rules, 2011 on t he Table of the Lok 
Sabha/Rajya Sabha is regretted.” 
 
 The Committee is not convinced with the reasons giv en by the 
Ministry of Urban Development that Notification cou ld not be laid in time 
due to curtailment of the Budget Session. Committee  impress upon the 
Ministry of Urban Development to endeavour to lay the Notification at the 
first available opportunity on the Table of the Hou se so as to fulfil 
statutory obligation. 
 
The Committee time and again have emphasized that l aying of 
rules/regulations/orders is a statutory obligation and should be completed 
on priority basis within specified time-frame. The Ministry of Urban 
Development should understand the implication of su ch failures. 
However, the Ministry of Urban Development have not  complied with the 
recommendations of the Committee in this regard. Th e Committee once 
again emphasise that Ministry of Urban Development should adhere to 
the time schedule in laying of notifications as pre scribed in Committee’s 
131 
st  Report. 
 
3. The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/ Departments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
,135 
th 
, 152 nd  
and 192 nd  Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immedia tely following the date 
of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette  and (ii) if the House is 
in Session, on the date of the publication of the O rder, during its 

 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than  15 clear days, before the 
expiry of the Session immediately following the sai d Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying o f the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Stat utory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably app end a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid s o as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay state ment the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be 
assigned a distinctive number in order to give it a  separate identity and 
similarly, no notification should be published/laid  which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee expects all Mini stries/Departments 
of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. In case where 
there are more than one notification under a single  file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number on each 
notification should be suitably distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay 
in laying of Notifications on the Table of the Hous e, the Committee also 
express their deep concern over delay in framing of  rules/regulations 
under different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented to the 
House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-ma king process 
should be completed within a period of six months of the coming into force 
on an Act. The committee has further recommended th at in case a 
Ministry is not able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek extension of 

 
time for completing the rule-making process. The re commendation of the 
committee reads as follows:- 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould 
well have been completed within the time limit of s ix months which 
the Committee has laid down for making of rules under an Act after 
coming into force of that Act. Where however, a Min istry does not 
find it possible to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the 
time limit and seek extension of time for completin g the rule-
making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with 
the Committee’s recommendation to complete the proc ess of framing of 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts of Parliament 
within a period of six months. At the same time, th e Committee also does 
not receive requests for extension of time for comp leting the rule-making 
process in terms of its recommendations as above fr om most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The committee takes a serio us note of the 
prevailing situation in which the Ministries/Depart ments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo -motu approach the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee further notes 
that in order to ensure timely framing of rules/reg ulations it has taken an 
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of su bordinate legislation in 
respect of all legislations brought about by differ ent 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India from the year 2003 
onwards with a view to ensure that the framing of s ubordinate legislation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise 
undertaken on behalf of the Committee.  

 
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates 
its recommendation that the Ministries/Departments should ensure 
putting in place subordinate legislation positively  within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee further 
recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they 
should invariably approach the Committee for seekin g extension of time. 
The Committee further recommends that in cases wher e the time limit of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying rules/regulations 
before the Parliament invariably lay a statement ex plaining the reasons 
why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed be yond six months so as 
to keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance o f the Parliament’s 
mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)

At the outset the Chairperson welcomed the new Memb ers nominated to the Committee.  
Thereafter, the Committee considered the draft 197 
th  Report  on Statutory Orders Laid on the Table 
of the Rajya Sabha during its 223 rd  Session and took note of the delay in the framing of rules/ 
regulations under the different Acts by the various  Ministries/ Departments.  The Committee was of 
the view that the Ministries/ Departments should se riously take the laying of papers in Parliament.  
The Committee decided that in cases where the time limit of six months was not adhered to by the 
Ministries/ Departments for framing the necessary s ubordinate legislation, the Ministries/ 
Departments should invariably inform the Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules 
within the time limit, justify the reasons for delay and seek extension of time for completing the rule 
making process.  The Committee, accordingly, decide d to hear the defaulting Ministries in the 
matter by calling the Secretary of the particular M inistries alongwith the Secretary, Ministry of 

Parliamentary Affairs before the Committee.  Therea fter, the Committee adopted the 197 th  Report 
unanimously.  The Committee decided to present the report to the House on the 17 th  May, 2012 and 
authorized the Chairperson and in her absence Shri Vijay Jawaharlal Darda and Dr. Janardhan 
Waghmare to present the report to the House.  
 
2. Thereafter, the Committee took up the issue of g iving retrospective effect to modifications 
in subordinate legislation as proposed by Shri K.N.  Balagopal, M.P. The Committee had 
preliminary discussion on the matter and were of th e view that the matter called for some research. 
Some Members were of the opinion that the matter ma y be referred to the Ministry of Law & 
Justice for their comments.  The Committee, however , decided to defer the matter and take it up for 
detailed discussion at its next meeting before taking a final decision.
